newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait Oil Co says in talks with trade union.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait Oil Co says in talks with trade union.

text.p: State-owned Kuwait Oil Co (KOC) said on Sunday it was in talks with its workers' union which has warned of a possible strike over promotions.
"The company (KOC) is continuing to meet the workers' union to discuss workers' issues and present its opinion about them," KOC said in a statement.
Union chairman Mohammad al-Sarhan told Reuters on Thursday the union was considering a possible strike in May over disputes with KOC about promotions.
In March 1995 the union launched a strike aimed at halting Kuwait's three percent share of world production to demand a reshuffle of employment grades.
The conditions of about 750 KOC export, maintenance, and gas operations workers need to be fixed, Sarhan has said.
KOC is the production arm of the state-owned conglomerate Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC), which oversees the oil industry.
OPEC member Kuwait produces about 2.0 million barrels of crude a day.
